lessons.title: Creating a TikTok Account for Reselling
lessons.body: To start selling on TikTok, you need a business account. Download TikTok from Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Open the app and sign up using your phone number or email. Use a phone number that you check often because TikTok sends verification codes. After signing up, go to your profile and tap the three lines at the top right. Select 'Settings and privacy', then 'Account', then 'Switch to Business Account'. Choose 'Business' and select a category like 'Shopping and Retail' or 'Product/Service'. This gives you access to analytics, including how many people view your videos and their demographics. Use a clear profile photo, like your logo or a picture of yourself holding your product. Write a bio that tells people what you sell and how to order. For example: 'Quality sneakers in Lagos. DM to order. Pay on delivery.' Add a link to your WhatsApp or Instagram if you have one. In your settings, enable 'Allow others to find me' and 'Allow direct messages' so customers can contact you. Also set up two-factor authentication for security. If you plan to use TikTok Shop, you will need to connect it later, but for now, focus on building your presence. Post your first video within 24 hours of creating the account. TikTok's algorithm favours new accounts that post consistently. Aim to post at least once a day for the first week. Use hashtags like #TikTokMadeMeBuyIt, #ShopSmall, and #AfricanBusiness. Engage with other sellers by commenting on their videos. This helps you learn and get noticed. Remember, your account is your shop. Keep it professional but friendly. Respond to comments and messages quickly. In Africa, many successful resellers started with just a phone and a few products. You can do the same.

lessons.title: Filming Engaging Product Videos
lessons.body: Your product videos must grab attention in the first 3 seconds. Use your smartphone camera. Natural light is best: film near a window during the day, or outside in the shade. Avoid direct sunlight as it creates harsh shadows. Clean your lens before filming. For product demos, show the item in use. If you sell clothes, wear them and show how they fit. If you sell phone accessories, plug them in and show them working. Use a tripod or stack books to keep your phone steady. Film in short clips of 5-10 seconds each, then edit them together in TikTok or CapCut. Add text overlays to highlight key points: price, size, colour, and how to order. Speak clearly in English or a local language your audience understands. Keep videos between 15 and 30 seconds. Longer videos work for tutorials but not for quick sales. Use trending sounds from TikTok's sound library. To find them, tap 'Add sound' and look for songs with an arrow icon. Show the product from different angles. For example, for a handbag, show the front, inside, and strap. Include a call to action: 'DM me to order' or 'Click the link in my bio'. Post at times when your audience is active. In many African countries, peak times are 7-9 AM, 1-2 PM, and 7-10 PM. Test different times. Use hashtags: #TikTokMadeMeBuyIt, #ShopSmallBusiness, #AfricanFashion, #LagosMarket. Respond to comments with video replies to boost engagement. If someone asks a question, make a video answering it. This creates more content and builds trust. Always show the real product, not stock photos. Customers want to see what they will get. If you dropship, order a sample first to film. For handmade items, show the process. People love seeing how things are made. Keep your background clean and uncluttered. A simple wall or fabric works well. Add captions for people watching without sound. Use TikTok's auto-captions or add them manually. Finally, be consistent. Post at least one video daily. The more you post, the better you get and the more the algorithm favours you.

lessons.title: Using TikTok Trends to Boost Sales
lessons.body: TikTok trends are challenges, sounds, or formats that many users copy. Using them can get your product seen by more people. To find trends, open TikTok and tap the 'For You' page. Look for videos with a music note icon and an arrow. Also check the 'Discover' tab for hashtags like #TikTokMadeMeBuyIt, #Trending, #Challenge. When you see a trend, think about how to adapt it to your product. For example, the 'What I ordered vs What I got' trend is perfect for showing real products. Film a split screen: on one side, the product photo from your supplier; on the other, the actual item you received. This builds trust. Another trend is 'Things TikTok Made Me Buy' where you show items you bought because of TikTok. You can feature your own product as if you bought it. Use trending sounds even if they are in another language; the algorithm promotes them. But make sure the sound fits your video. For dance trends, you can dance while holding your product. For text-based trends, like 'Tell me you're a reseller without telling me', write text on screen and show your products. Participate in challenges like #SmallBusinessCheck where you show your workspace. Always add your own twist. Don't just copy; make it relevant to your product. Use 3-5 hashtags per video: one broad (#TikTokMadeMeBuyIt), one niche (#AfricanPrint), one location (#NairobiBusiness). Post your trend video within 24-48 hours of the trend peaking. Use TikTok's 'Analytics' to see which trends drive views to your profile. If a trend works, make more videos with it. Engage with other users' trend videos by commenting and duetting. Duetting means you film your reaction alongside their video. If someone shows a problem your product solves, duet it and show your solution. This puts your product in front of their audience. Be careful not to jump on trends that don't match your brand. For example, a serious business might avoid silly dance trends. But for many resellers, fun trends work well. Track your results: use TikTok's built-in analytics to see views, likes, shares, and profile visits. If a trend brings sales, note it. If not, try another. Trends change fast, so check daily. Set aside 15 minutes each morning to scroll and find trends. Save sounds you might use. Then film your version. Consistency is key: even if a trend doesn't go viral, it keeps your account active.

lessons.title: Going Live on TikTok to Sell
lessons.body: TikTok Live lets you sell in real time. You need at least 1,000 followers to go live. To start, tap the '+' button at the bottom, then swipe to 'LIVE'. Before going live, plan your session. Choose 5-10 products to show. Write down key details: price, sizes, colours, and any discounts. Set up your filming area with good lighting and a clean background. Use a tripod or prop your phone. Test your internet connection; a stable Wi-Fi or 4G is best. Tell your followers in advance by posting a video or story: 'Going live at 7 PM to show new arrivals. Don't miss it!' During the live, greet viewers by name. Show each product clearly. Demonstrate how it works. Mention the price and how to order: 'DM me the word "BUY" and your size.' Offer live-only discounts to encourage immediate purchases. For example, 'First 5 buyers get 10% off.' Use a countdown timer for flash sales. Interact with comments: answer questions, thank people for gifts, and acknowledge shares. If someone buys, shout them out: 'Thank you, Ama from Accra, for buying the red dress!' This encourages others. Keep the energy high. Speak clearly and enthusiastically. You can also do giveaways: 'I'll give a free gift to one person who shares this live.' To receive payments, share your mobile money number or payment link in the comments. For TikTok Shop, you can add products to your live so viewers can tap to buy. After the live, review the recording to see what worked. TikTok saves your live for 30 days. Post clips from the live as regular videos to reach more people. Go live at least twice a week. Consistency builds an audience. In Africa, many sellers go live in the evening when people are home. Test different times to see when you get the most viewers. Use a wired earphone with a mic for better audio. Keep a notepad to track orders. After the live, send payment details to buyers and confirm their orders. Ship quickly to build trust. Live selling is powerful because it creates urgency and personal connection. With practice, you can sell out your stock in one session.

lessons.title: TikTok Shop Setup and Integration
lessons.body: TikTok Shop lets you sell directly in the app. It is available in some African countries like South Africa, Nigeria, and Kenya, but check if it's available in yours. To set up, go to your profile, tap the three lines, then 'Settings and privacy', then 'Account', then 'TikTok Shop'. Follow the prompts to register as a seller. You will need a business license or ID, a bank account or mobile money account, and product photos. If TikTok Shop is not available in your country, you can still use other methods: add a link to your WhatsApp or Instagram in your bio, or use a third-party link like Linktree. For TikTok Shop, once approved, you can list products. Each listing needs a title, description, price, and up to 9 images. Use clear photos and include keywords in the title, like 'Men's Leather Shoes Size 42-45'. Set shipping options: you can ship yourself or use TikTok's logistics partners. Offer free shipping if possible; it increases sales. You can also run promotions like discounts and bundles. To integrate with your videos, when you film, tap 'Add link' and select your product. Viewers can then tap the product icon to buy. In live videos, you can pin products so viewers can shop while watching. Use TikTok's analytics to track views, clicks, and sales. If a product isn't selling, change the photos or price. Respond to customer messages within 24 hours. Ship orders within 2-3 days. Good reviews boost your shop's ranking. Ask buyers to leave a review after delivery. If you don't have TikTok Shop, you can still use TikTok to drive sales to your WhatsApp. Put your WhatsApp link in your bio and say 'DM to order'. Use a WhatsApp Business account to automate replies and catalogue products. Many African resellers use this method successfully. For payments, mobile money like M-Pesa, MTN MoMo, and Airtel Money are common. Always confirm payment before shipping. Keep records of orders and expenses. As you grow, consider registering your business for legal protection. TikTok Shop is a powerful tool, but even without it, you can sell effectively by directing traffic to your preferred platform.

lessons.title: Building a Following for Repeat Sales
lessons.body: To get repeat sales, you need a loyal following. Start by posting consistently. Aim for 1-2 videos daily. Use a content mix: 60% entertaining or educational, 30% product showcases, 10% personal stories. For example, show how you package orders, share customer reviews, or give tips on choosing products. Engage with your audience. Reply to every comment within a few hours. Like and reply to DMs. Ask questions in your videos: 'Which colour do you prefer?' This encourages comments and boosts your video. Collaborate with other small businesses. Do shoutouts for shoutouts: you promote their product, they promote yours. This exposes you to new audiences. Use TikTok's 'Duet' and 'Stitch' features to interact with other creators. Stitch means you clip a small part of their video and add your own commentary. If a customer posts a video using your product, duet it and thank them. This makes them feel valued and encourages others to post. Run contests: 'Tag 3 friends in the comments to win a free gift.' This increases reach. Offer a loyalty program: 'Buy 3 items, get 1 free' or 'Repeat customers get 10% off.' Keep a customer list (with permission) and send them WhatsApp messages about new stock. Use TikTok's 'Analytics' to see your top viewers' locations and times. Post when they are most active. Use hashtags that your audience follows: #TikTokMadeMeBuyIt, #ShopSmall, #AfricanBusiness, #SupportLocal. Create a series: 'Day 1 of building my fashion business' or 'Pack an order with me.' Series keep people coming back. Show your face and personality. People buy from people they trust. Share your struggles and wins. Be authentic. If you make a mistake, apologise and fix it. Good customer service leads to repeat sales. After a sale, follow up: 'Did you receive your order? How is it?' Ask for a review. Offer a discount on their next purchase. Build a community, not just a customer base. Respond to negative comments politely and take conversations to DM. Finally, be patient. Building a following takes time. Many successful African TikTok sellers started with zero followers. Post, learn, and improve. Celebrate small wins. With consistency, you will build a loyal following that buys from you again and again.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: TikTok Shop Setup, Payments, and Order Fulfilment for African Resellers

This practical reference supports Module 5 of Rise Africa Skills â Reselling on Social Media Platforms. It is written for resellers who already know how to create content, build a following, and go live. The focus here is the operational backbone that turns views into cash: setting up TikTok Shop correctly, understanding payment flows and settlement in African markets, and building a fulfilment routine that protects your seller rating and your margins.

Across Africa, social commerce is growing faster than formal retail infrastructure. A reseller in Accra, Lagos, Nairobi, or Kampala can reach thousands of buyers with a phone and a data bundle. But the businesses that survive are not the ones with the most viral videos â they are the ones that can take an order, collect payment, dispatch stock, and handle returns without losing money. This lesson gives you the numbers, the process, and the checklists to do exactly that.

Why Fulfilment Decides Whether You Make Money

Most new resellers obsess over content and ignore logistics. That is backwards. A video that gets 50,000 views but leads to 40 orders you cannot pack on time will destroy your shop rating faster than a video with 2,000 views and 10 clean deliveries. On TikTok Shop, your seller rating is driven by order defect rate, late dispatch, and cancellation rate. In most markets, a shop that drops below a threshold on these metrics loses visibility in the algorithm â meaning your content stops being shown to buyers.

The practical rule: only scale your content when your fulfilment can absorb the volume. If you can pack and dispatch 15 orders a day reliably, do not run a promotion designed to generate 100 orders a day. Build in batches.

Payments and Settlement in African Markets

TikTok Shop availability and payment methods vary by country. In markets where TikTok Shop is live, sellers typically link a local bank account or a supported mobile money wallet for settlement. Where TikTok Shop is not yet available, most African resellers use a hybrid model: content and live selling on TikTok, order capture via WhatsApp or Instagram DM, and payment via mobile money (M-Pesa, MTN MoMo, Airtel Money, Orange Money) or bank transfer.

Understanding mobile money transaction costs is essential because they eat directly into margin. The table below shows representative mobile money and card transaction costs across selected African markets. Figures are indicative and change frequently â always confirm current tariffs with your provider.

Table 1: Indicative Digital Payment Costs in Selected African Markets
Market Common Payment Method Typical Cost to Seller/User Notes
Kenya M-Pesa (Safaricom) ~0â1.5% of transaction value depending on tier Free for many small person-to-person transfers; merchant tariffs differ
Ghana MTN MoMo / Telecel Cash ~1â2% merchant transaction fee (varies) E-levy historically applied to electronic transactions; verify current rules
Nigeria Bank transfer / USSD / POS ~0.5â1.5% or flat fee per transfer Card and transfer fees vary by bank and channel
Uganda MTN MoMo / Airtel Money ~1â2% withdrawal and merchant fees Withdrawal fees are a common hidden cost for resellers
South Africa Card / EFT / SnapScan ~1.5â3.5% card processing Card fees higher than mobile money in many cases

Sources: GSMA, State of the Industry Report on Mobile Money (annual editions); Central Bank of Kenya tariff disclosures; Bank of Ghana payment systems data. Figures are indicative ranges for planning purposes only.

The key takeaway: if your product margin is 20% and payment costs are 2%, delivery is 8%, and returns run at 5%, you are left with roughly 5% net. That is why pricing must be built from the bottom up, not guessed.

Building a Fulfilment Routine That Scales

A reliable fulfilment routine has five stages: order confirmation, stock check, packing, dispatch, and follow-up. Each stage should have a fixed time slot in your day. Successful resellers in Nairobi and Lagos typically batch these: confirm and pack orders in the morning, dispatch by midday, follow up in the evening.

Delivery is often the largest controllable cost. The table below compares common last-mile options used by African social commerce sellers. Costs are indicative and vary by city and distance.

Table 2: Indicative Last-Mile Delivery Options for African Resellers
Delivery Option Typical Cost (indicative) Speed Best For
Boda / motorcycle courier (direct) USD 1â3 per local delivery Same day High-value, same-city orders
Third-party courier aggregator (e.g. Sendy, Kwik, GIG) USD 2â5 per delivery Same to next day Volume orders, tracking required
Bus / matatu parcel service USD 0.50â2 per parcel 1â2 days intercity Low-cost intercity, non-fragile goods
Pickup point / locker USD 0.30â1.50 per parcel 1â3 days Cost-conscious buyers, urban areas
Postal service USD 0.50â3 per parcel 3â10 days Remote areas, low-value items

Sources: World Bank, Africa's Pulse and logistics performance data; national postal and courier operator tariff sheets; market rates reported by social commerce operators in Kenya, Nigeria, and Ghana. Costs are indicative planning figures and should be verified locally.

Managing Returns Without Losing Your Margin

Returns are normal in e-commerce, but in social commerce they can be brutal because your content created an emotional purchase. Three practices reduce return rates:

  • Show the product honestly on camera. Zoom in on stitching, fabric, size, and flaws. Buyers who know what they are getting return less.
  • State size and fit clearly in every video. "This runs small â order one size up" prevents a large share of returns.
  • Confirm the order before dispatch. A 30-second WhatsApp voice note confirming colour, size, and address costs almost nothing and prevents costly failed deliveries.

Set a clear, written return policy and put it in your TikTok bio and order confirmation message. Ambiguity creates disputes; disputes damage your shop rating.

SAFETY WARNING â RESTRICTED AND REGULATED PRODUCTS

Do not sell medicines, veterinary drugs, pesticides, unregistered cosmetics, food supplements making health claims, or any product requiring regulatory approval through TikTok Shop or social media unless you hold the required licence and the product is registered with your national regulator (e.g. NAFDAC in Nigeria, PPB in Kenya, FDA Ghana, SAHPRA in South Africa). Selling unregistered or counterfeit health, agricultural, or chemical products is illegal, can seriously harm buyers and animals, and exposes you to prosecution and permanent platform bans. If a supplier offers you "fast-moving" medicines, agrochemicals, or slimming products at unusually low prices, treat it as a red flag. Verify registration numbers directly with the national regulator before listing.

Quick Reference Checklist

  1. Confirm TikTok Shop or hybrid model for your country before promising buyers a checkout method.
  2. Link a verified payout account (bank or mobile money) and confirm settlement timing in your seller dashboard.
  3. Calculate your true margin: selling price â cost of goods â platform fee â payment fee â delivery â expected returns.
  4. Set a daily packing capacity and do not run promotions that exceed it.
  5. Batch your day: confirm and pack in the morning, dispatch by midday, follow up in the evening.
  6. Confirm every order in writing (WhatsApp or DM) with colour, size, and address before dispatch.
  7. Publish a clear return policy in your bio and order confirmation message.
  8. Never list restricted products (medicines, agrochemicals, unregistered cosmetics) without a valid licence and registration.

Further Reading

  • GSMA â State of the Industry Report on Mobile Money: https://www.gsma.com/sotir/
  • FAO â Digital Technologies in Agriculture and Rural Areas: https://www.fao.org/documents/card/en/c/ca4985en
  • World Bank â Africa's Pulse (economic and trade data): https://www.worldbank.org/en/publication/africas-pulse
  • TikTok Seller University â Shop setup and policy guides: https://seller-us.tiktok.com/university
  • WHO â Guidance on regulation of health products and online sales: https://www.who.int/teams/regulation-prequalification

Bottom line: In African social commerce, the reseller who controls fulfilment controls the business. Content gets attention; payments, packing, and delivery get paid. Build the operational backbone first, then scale the content to match it.

quiz.q: What type of TikTok account should you create for reselling?
quiz.explanation: A business account gives you access to analytics and features useful for selling.

quiz.q: Where can you switch to a business account on TikTok?
quiz.explanation: The option to switch account type is under 'Settings and privacy' then 'Account'.

quiz.q: What should your TikTok bio include for reselling?
options: B) What you sell and how to order
quiz.explanation: The bio should clearly state your products and how customers can contact you.

quiz.q: Why is it important to enable direct messages on your TikTok account?
options: B) To let customers contact you
quiz.explanation: Direct messages allow potential buyers to ask questions and place orders.

quiz.q: How soon after creating your TikTok account should you post your first video?
quiz.explanation: Posting within 24 hours helps the algorithm notice your new account.

quiz.q: What is the best lighting for filming product videos?
options: B) Natural light from a window
quiz.explanation: Natural light from a window provides soft, even lighting without harsh shadows.

quiz.q: What should you do before filming a product video?
quiz.explanation: A clean lens ensures clear, sharp video quality.

quiz.q: What is a good length for a product video on TikTok?
quiz.explanation: Short videos of 15-30 seconds are more engaging and easier to watch.

quiz.q: What should you include in your video to tell viewers how to buy?
quiz.explanation: A call to action like 'DM to order' tells viewers what to do next.

quiz.q: Why should you use trending sounds in your videos?
options: A) They are the only sounds available
B) They can increase your video's reach
C) They are required by TikTok
D) They are always in English
quiz.explanation: TikTok's algorithm often promotes videos that use trending sounds.

quiz.q: What is a good time to post on TikTok in many African countries?
quiz.explanation: These are peak times when many users are active on the app.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of replying to comments with a video?
options: A) It creates more content and boosts engagement
C) It takes too much time
quiz.explanation: Video replies create additional content and encourage more interaction.

quiz.q: How can you find trending sounds on TikTok?
options: A) Tap 'Add sound' and look for the arrow icon
quiz.explanation: Sounds with an arrow icon are trending and can boost your video's visibility.

quiz.q: What is the 'What I ordered vs What I got' trend useful for?
options: A) Showing real products and building trust
quiz.explanation: This trend lets you show the actual product and reassure buyers about quality.

quiz.q: What does 'duetting' mean on TikTok?
options: A) Filming your reaction alongside another video
B) Posting two videos at once
quiz.explanation: Duetting allows you to create a split-screen video with another user's content.

quiz.q: How many hashtags should you use per video?
quiz.explanation: Using 3-5 relevant hashtags is effective without looking spammy.

quiz.q: What should you do if a trend doesn't match your brand?
quiz.explanation: Only participate in trends that align with your product and audience.

quiz.q: How many followers do you need to go live on TikTok?
quiz.explanation: TikTok requires at least 1,000 followers to access the LIVE feature.

quiz.q: What should you do before going live?
options: A) Plan your products and prices
quiz.explanation: Planning helps you stay organised and sell more effectively during the live.

quiz.q: How can you encourage immediate purchases during a live?
quiz.explanation: Live-only discounts create urgency and motivate viewers to buy now.

quiz.q: What should you do after a live session?
options: A) Review the recording and post clips
quiz.explanation: Posting clips from the live reaches more people and extends the content's life.

quiz.q: What is needed to set up TikTok Shop?
options: A) A business license or ID
quiz.explanation: TikTok Shop requires verification documents like a business license or ID.

quiz.q: How can you sell on TikTok if TikTok Shop is not available in your country?
options: A) Use WhatsApp link in bio
quiz.explanation: Directing viewers to WhatsApp is a common alternative for African resellers.

quiz.q: What should you do after a customer places an order on TikTok Shop?
quiz.explanation: Fast shipping builds trust and leads to positive reviews.

quiz.q: Why are good reviews important for your TikTok Shop?
options: A) They boost your shop's ranking
D) They are required by law
quiz.explanation: Positive reviews improve your shop's visibility and credibility.

quiz.q: What content mix is recommended for building a following?
quiz.explanation: This mix keeps your audience engaged while still promoting your products.

quiz.q: What is a good way to engage your audience?
options: D) Only post once a month
quiz.explanation: Quick replies show you care and encourage more interaction.

quiz.q: What is a loyalty program?
quiz.explanation: Loyalty programs like 'buy 3 get 1 free' encourage repeat purchases.

quiz.q: Why should you show your face in videos?
options: A) People buy from people they trust
B) It is required by TikTok
quiz.explanation: Showing your face builds personal connection and trust with your audience.

quiz.q: What should you do after a sale to encourage repeat business?
options: A) Follow up and ask for a review
quiz.explanation: Following up shows good service and can lead to repeat sales and reviews.
